Definition: from G3173; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection:--great things, wonderful works.
BiblicalUsage: The word means magnificent things, and Luke uses it once, at Pentecost, where the crowd hears the apostles speak in their own tongues the wonderful works of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wonderful works are the sign of the new age: the Spirit gives plain men the words of God, and the crowd hears the greatness of God in its own tongue.
